source: May et al. (2021), AJ 162, 158, 'Spitzer Phase-curve Observations and Circulation Models of the Inflated Ultrahot Jupiter WASP-76b' (doi:10.3847/1538-3881/ac0e30; arXiv:2107.03349). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um phase curve wa076bo21, 15-17 April 2017, program 13038. Values read from the authors' LaTeX source: section 3 and appendix Table 4 (table:all_params), column wa076bo21.

model.description: SPIDERMAN spherical harmonics, second order: 'we only consider the two terms that create a dipole centered at a latitude and longitude of zero degrees, and use SPIDERMAN's longitude offset parameter' (section 2.2). Table 4 lists sph0 (Y00) and sph3 (Y11); the two other second-order terms are zero. Its note: 'We use the lon0/lat0 options in spiderman'.

spiderman.lo0Reading: Table 4 prints lo0 = 0.67 [deg]. SPIDERMAN takes radians, so the fit passed 0.67 degrees = 0.011694 rad: read as 0.67 rad, the map's day side is 3,423 ppm after the dilution correction and the half amplitude 1,266 ppm, far from the paper's 3,729 and 1,464 ppm; read as 0.67 degrees they are 3,704 and 1,546 ppm. In spiderman-package 1.0.3 the lo0 slot moves the dipole in latitude, not longitude (see the WASP-76b README).

dilution.where: section 2.3, dilution factor at 4.5 um for the companion WASP-76 B

daysideK.where: section 3.3, disk-integrated day side brightness temperature (Kurucz stellar model, Teff 6250 K, log g 4.13, [Fe/H] 0.23)

semiAmplitude.where: section 3.3; the paper does not say whether this is half the peak-to-peak or whether it is dilution corrected
